verses.1:1: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and laid siege to it.
verses.1:2: And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, and part of the vessels of the house of God, and he brought them into the land of Shinar, of the house of his god, and the vessels he brought into the treasury house of his god.
verses.1:3: And the king told Ashpenaz his chief eunuch to bring in from the sons of the captivity of Israel, and from the royal seed, and from the nobles,
verses.1:4: young men in whom there is no blemish, and handsome in appearance, and having understanding in all wisdom, and knowing knowledge, and comprehending insight, and in whom there is strength to stand in the king's house, and to teach them the writings and language of the Chaldeans.
verses.1:5: And the king appointed for them the day's portion day by day from the king's table and from the wine of his drinking, and to nourish them for three years, and after these things to stand before the king.
verses.1:6: And there were among them, from the sons of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
verses.1:7: And the chief eunuch gave names to them: to Daniel, Belteshazzar; and to Hananiah, Shadrach; and to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
verses.1:8: And Daniel set it upon his heart that he would not be defiled by the king's table and by the wine of his drinking, and he entreated the chief eunuch that he would not be defiled.
verses.1:9: And God gave Daniel into mercy and compassion before the chief eunuch.
verses.1:10: And the chief eunuch said to Daniel, "I fear my lord the king, who appointed your food and your drink, in case he sees your faces gloomy compared to the youths of your own age, and you condemn my head to the king."
verses.1:11: And Daniel said to Amelsad, whom the chief eunuch had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, Azariah:
verses.1:12: "Please test your servants for ten days, and let them give us some of the seeds, and we will eat, and we will drink water;
verses.1:13: and let our appearances be seen before you, and the appearances of the youths who eat from the king's table, and just as you see, deal with your servants."
verses.1:14: And he listened to them, and tested them for ten days.
verses.1:15: And after the end of the ten days, their appearances were seen to be good, and they were strong in their flesh, more than the youths who were eating from the king's table.
verses.1:16: And Amelsad continued taking away their dinner and the wine of their drink, and giving them seeds.
verses.1:17: And as for these youths, the four of them, God gave them understanding and insight in all literature and wisdom; and Daniel had understanding in every vision and dreams.
verses.1:18: And after the end of the days that the king had said to bring them in, then the chief eunuch brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.1:19: And the king spoke with them, and among all of them there were not found any like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; and they stood before the king.
verses.1:20: And in every matter of wisdom and knowledge about which the king inquired from them, he found them tenfold beyond all the enchanters and the magicians who were in all his kingdom.
verses.1:21: And Daniel remained until the first year of Cyrus the king.
verses.2:1: In the second year of the reign, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed a dream, and his spirit was distraught, and his sleep went from him.
verses.2:2: And the king said to call the enchanters and the magicians and the sorcerers and the Chaldeans to report to the king his dreams; and they came and stood before the king.
verses.2:3: And the king said to them, "I dreamed, and my spirit was distraught to know the dream."
verses.2:4: And the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic, "King, live forever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will report the interpretation."
verses.2:5: The king answered the Chaldeans, "The word has departed from me; if you do not make known to me the dream and the interpretation, you will be for destruction, and your houses will be plundered.
verses.2:6: But if you make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts and presents and great honor; only report to me the dream and its interpretation."
verses.2:7: They answered a second time and said, "Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will report its interpretation."
verses.2:8: And the king answered and said, "Truly I know that you are buying time, because you have seen that the matter has departed from me.
verses.2:9: So if you do not report the dream to me, I know that you have agreed to speak a false and corrupt word before me until the time passes. Tell me my dream, and I will know that you will report its interpretation to me."
verses.2:10: The Chaldeans answered before the king and said, "There is no man on the dry land who will be able to make known the matter of the king, because no great king or ruler asks such a matter of an enchanter, magician, or Chaldean.
verses.2:11: For the word which the king asks is heavy, and there is no other who will report it before the king except gods, whose dwelling is not with any flesh."
verses.2:12: Then the king in fury and anger said to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:13: And the decree went out, and the wise men were being killed; and they sought Daniel and his friends to do away with them.
verses.2:14: Then Daniel answered with counsel and judgment to Arioch, the king's chief cook, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon:
verses.2:15: "Officer of the king, why has this shameless judgment gone out from the presence of the king?" Then Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.
verses.2:16: And Daniel asked the king to give him time, and he would report its interpretation to the king.
verses.2:17: And Daniel went into his house, and made the matter known to Hananiah and Mishael and Azariah, his friends.
verses.2:18: And they sought compassion from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his friends might not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:19: Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night. And Daniel blessed the God of heaven
verses.2:20: and said, "May the name of God be blessed from age to age, because wisdom and understanding are His.
verses.2:21: And He changes seasons and times; He sets up kings and removes them, giving wisdom to the wise and prudence to those who know understanding.
verses.2:22: He reveals deep and hidden things, knowing what is in the darkness, and the light is with Him.
verses.2:23: To You, God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because You have given me wisdom and power, and You have made known to me what we asked of You, and You have made known to me the king's vision."
verses.2:24: And Daniel came to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, "Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon, but bring me in before the king, and I will report the interpretation to the king."
verses.2:25: Then Arioch in haste brought Daniel in before the king and said to him, "I have found a man from the sons of the captivity of Judea who will report the interpretation to the king."
verses.2:26: And the king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, "Are you able to report to me the dream that I saw and its interpretation?"
verses.2:27: And Daniel answered before the king and said, "The mystery which the king asks about is not for wise men, magicians, enchanters, or diviners to report to the king;
verses.2:28: but there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what must come to pass in the last days. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed, this is it.
verses.2:29: King, your thoughts upon your bed rose up about what must come to pass after these things, and He who reveals mysteries has made known to you what must come to pass.
verses.2:30: And as for me, not by any wisdom that is in me beyond all the living has this mystery been revealed to me, but for the purpose of making the interpretation known to the king, so that you may know the thoughts of your heart.
verses.2:31: You, King, were watching, and look, a single image. That image was great, and its look was extraordinary as it stood before your face, and the sight of it was fearsome.
verses.2:32: It was an image whose head was of fine gold, its hands and chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze,
verses.2:33: its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of earthenware.
verses.2:34: You were watching until a stone was cut off from a mountain without hands, and it struck the image on its feet of iron and earthenware, and pulverized them completely.
verses.2:35: Then the earthenware, the iron, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were pulverized all at once, and became like dust from a summer threshing floor; and the full force of the wind carried them away, and no place was found for them. And the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
verses.2:36: This is the dream; and its interpretation we will tell before the king.
verses.2:37: You, King, king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given a kingdom strong and mighty and honored
verses.2:38: in every place where the sons of men dwell; both the wild animals of the field and the birds of heaven He has given into your hand, and He has appointed you lord of all; you are the head of gold.
verses.2:39: And after you another kingdom will arise, inferior to you, and a third kingdom, which is the bronze, which will rule over all the earth.
verses.2:40: And a fourth kingdom will be strong as iron; in the way that iron pulverizes and subdues all things, so it will pulverize and subdue all things.
verses.2:41: And whereas you saw the feet and the toes partly of earthenware and partly of iron, it will be a divided kingdom, and some of the root of iron will be in it, just as you saw the iron mixed with the earthenware.
verses.2:42: And as the toes of the feet were partly of iron and partly of earthenware, part of the kingdom will be strong, and part of it will be broken.
verses.2:43: Whereas you saw the iron mixed with the earthenware, they will be mixed together by the seed of men; but they will not cling one to the other, just as iron does not mix with earthenware.
verses.2:44: And in the days of those kings the God of heaven will raise up a kingdom which will never be destroyed, and His kingdom will not be left to another people; it will pulverize and winnow all the kingdoms, and it will stand up forever,
verses.2:45: just as you saw that a stone was cut from a mountain without hands, and it pulverized the earthenware, the iron, the bronze, the silver, and the gold. The great God has made known to the king what must come to pass after these things; and the dream is true, and its interpretation is trustworthy."
verses.2:46: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and worshiped Daniel, and he gave orders to pour out an offering and fragrant incense to him.
verses.2:47: And the king answered and said to Daniel, "Truly your God, He is God of gods and Lord of kings and a revealer of mysteries, because you were able to reveal this mystery."
verses.2:48: And the king made Daniel great, and gave him many great gifts, and appointed him over the whole province of Babylon and as chief of satraps over all the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:49: And Daniel made a request of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon; and Daniel was in the court of the king.
verses.3:1: In the eighteenth year, Nebuchadnezzar the king made a golden image, its height was sixty cubits, its width six cubits; and he set it up in the plain of Deira, in the province of Babylon.
verses.3:2: And he sent to gather the chief magistrates and the commanders and the district governors, leaders and potentates and those in authority, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image that he had set up.
verses.3:3: And the district governors, chief magistrates, commanders, leaders, great potentates, those in authority, and all the rulers of the provinces were gathered to the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up. And they stood before the image.
verses.3:4: And the herald cried out with strength: "To you it is declared, peoples, tribes, languages,
verses.3:5: at whatever hour you hear the sound of the trumpet, pipe and lyre, trigon and psaltery, and every kind of music, fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king set up;
verses.3:6: and whoever does not worship, in that very hour will be thrown into the burning furnace of fire."
verses.3:7: And it happened when the peoples heard the sound of the trumpet, pipe and lyre, trigon and psaltery, and every kind of music, all the peoples, tribes, languages fell down and worshiped the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.
verses.3:8: Then Chaldean men came forward and accused the Jews to the king,
verses.3:10: You, king, issued a decree that every person who hears the sound of the trumpet, pipe and lyre, trigon and psaltery, and every kind of music,
verses.3:11: and does not fall down and worship the golden image, will be thrown into the burning furnace of fire.
verses.3:12: There are Jewish men whom you appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, who have not obeyed, king, your decree; they do not serve your gods and they do not worship the golden image that you set up."
verses.3:13: Then Nebuchadnezzar in fury and anger gave orders to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego; and they were brought before the king.
verses.3:14: And Nebuchadnezzar answered and said to them, "Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, that you do not serve my gods and do not worship the golden image that I set up?
verses.3:15: Now therefore, if you are ready, when you hear the sound of the trumpet, pipe and lyre, trigon and psaltery, and bagpipe, and every kind of music, to fall down and worship the image that I made—but if you do not worship, in that very hour you will be thrown into the burning furnace of fire. And who is a god who will rescue you out of my hand?"
verses.3:16: And Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego answered, saying to King Nebuchadnezzar, "We have no need to answer you concerning this matter.
verses.3:17: For there is a God, whom we serve, able to rescue us from the burning furnace of fire; and out of your hands, king, He will deliver us.
verses.3:18: And if not, let it be known to you, king, that we do not serve your gods and we do not worship the image that you set up."
verses.3:19: Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the appearance of his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and he gave orders to heat the furnace sevenfold, until it was completely heated.
verses.3:20: And he gave orders to men mighty in strength, after binding Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, to throw them into the burning furnace of fire.
verses.3:21: Then those men were bound with their trousers and turbans and leggings, and were thrown into the middle of the burning furnace of fire,
verses.3:22: because the king's word was urgent, and the furnace was heated exceedingly.
verses.3:23: And these three, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell into the middle of the burning furnace, bound.
verses.3:24: And they were walking about in the middle of the flame, singing hymns to God and blessing the Lord.
verses.3:25: And Azariah stood up and prayed in this way, and opening his mouth in the middle of the fire, he said,
verses.3:26: "Blessed are You, Lord, the God of our fathers, and praiseworthy, and glorified is Your name forever.
verses.3:27: For You are righteous in all that You have done, and all Your works are true, and Your ways are straight, and all Your judgments are truth.
verses.3:28: And You have executed judgments of truth according to all that You have brought upon us and upon the holy city of our fathers, Jerusalem; for in truth and judgment You have brought all these things because of our sins.
verses.3:29: For we have sinned and acted lawlessly in turning away from You, and we have sinned greatly in all things; and we have not listened to Your commandments,
verses.3:30: nor kept them, nor done as You commanded us, so that it might go well with us.
verses.3:31: And everything that You have brought upon us and everything that You have done to us, You have done in true judgment.
verses.3:32: And You have handed us over into the hands of lawless enemies and most hateful rebels, and to an unjust and most wicked king above all the earth.
verses.3:33: And now it is not possible for us to open our mouth; shame and reproach have come upon Your servants and upon those who revere You.
verses.3:34: Please do not hand us over completely for the sake of Your name, and do not annul Your covenant,
verses.3:35: and do not turn away Your mercy from us, for the sake of Abraham who is loved by You, and for the sake of Isaac Your servant and Israel Your holy one,
verses.3:36: to whom You spoke of multiplying their seed like the stars of heaven and like the sand along the shore of the sea.
verses.3:37: For, Master, we have been made smaller than all the nations, and we are lowly in all the earth today because of our sins.
verses.3:38: And there is not at this time ruler, or prophet, or leader, nor burnt offering, nor sacrifice, nor offering, nor incense, no place to offer sacrifice before You and find mercy.
verses.3:39: Yet with a broken soul and a spirit of humility may we be accepted; as with a burnt offering of rams and bulls, and with tens of thousands of fat lambs,
verses.3:40: so let our sacrifice be before You today and carry through completely after You, for there will be no shame for those who trust in You.
verses.3:41: And now we follow with a whole heart, and we fear You and seek Your face. Do not put us to shame,
verses.3:42: but deal with us according to Your gentleness and according to the abundance of Your mercy.
verses.3:43: And rescue us according to Your wonders, and give glory to Your name, Lord.
verses.3:44: And may all who show evil to Your servants be ashamed, and may they be put to shame from all their power, and may their strength be broken;
verses.3:45: let them know that You are the Lord God alone and glorious over the whole inhabited world."
verses.3:46: And the king's attendants who threw them in did not stop stoking the furnace with naphtha and pitch and tow and brushwood.
verses.3:47: and the flame spread out above the furnace for forty-nine cubits,
verses.3:48: and passed through and burned up those of the Chaldeans whom it found around the furnace.
verses.3:49: But the angel of the Lord went down together with Azariah and those with him into the furnace, and drove the flame of the fire out of the furnace,
verses.3:50: and made the middle of the furnace like a whistling wind of dew; and the fire did not touch them at all, and neither distressed nor troubled them.
verses.3:51: Then the three, as from one mouth, were singing hymns and glorifying and blessing God in the furnace, saying:
verses.3:52: "Blessed are You, Lord, the God of our fathers, and praiseworthy and highly exalted forever. And blessed is the holy name of Your glory, and supremely praiseworthy and highly exalted for all ages.
verses.3:53: Blessed are You in the temple of Your holy glory, and supremely worthy of hymns and supremely glorious forever.
verses.3:54: Blessed are You on the throne of Your kingdom, and supremely worthy of hymns and highly exalted forever.
verses.3:55: Blessed are You who look upon the depths, seated upon cherubim, and praiseworthy and highly exalted forever.
verses.3:56: Blessed are You in the expanse of heaven, and worthy of hymns and glorified forever.
verses.3:57: Bless the Lord, all works of the Lord; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:58: Bless the Lord, angels of the Lord; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:59: Bless the Lord, heavens; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:60: Bless the Lord, waters and all things above heaven; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:61: Let all the host bless the Lord; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:62: Bless the Lord, sun and moon; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:63: Bless the Lord, stars of heaven; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:64: Let all rain and dew bless the Lord; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:65: Bless the Lord, all winds; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:66: Bless the Lord, fire and heat; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:71: Bless the Lord, nights and days; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:72: Bless the Lord, light and darkness; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever. Bless the Lord, cold and heat; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever. Bless the Lord, frost and snow; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:73: Bless the Lord, lightnings and clouds; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:74: Let the earth bless the Lord; let it sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:75: Bless the Lord, mountains and hills; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:76: Bless the Lord, all things that grow on the earth; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:77: Bless the Lord, springs; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:78: Bless the Lord, seas and rivers; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:79: Bless the Lord, sea monsters and all things that move in the waters; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:80: Bless the Lord, all birds of the sky; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:81: Bless the Lord, all wild animals and livestock; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:82: Bless the Lord, sons of men; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:83: Bless the Lord, Israel; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:84: Bless the Lord, priests; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:85: Bless the Lord, servants; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:86: Bless the Lord, spirits and souls of the righteous; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:87: Bless the Lord, godly and humble in heart; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever.
verses.3:88: Bless the Lord, Hananiah, Azariah, Mishael; sing hymns to Him and highly exalt Him forever; for He has rescued us from Hades, and from the hand of death He has saved us, and He has delivered us from the middle of a burning furnace of flame, and from the middle of the fire He has delivered us.
verses.3:89: Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy is forever.
verses.3:90: Bless the God of gods, all who revere the Lord; sing hymns and give thanks, for His mercy is forever."
verses.3:91: And Nebuchadnezzar heard them singing hymns and was amazed, and he stood up in haste and said to his nobles, "Did we not throw three men into the middle of the fire, bound?" And they said to the king, "Truly, king."
verses.3:92: "Look, I see four men unbound and walking about in the middle of the fire, and there is no harm in them, and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of God."
verses.3:93: Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the door of the burning furnace of fire and said, "Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out and come here." And Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego came out from the middle of the fire.
verses.3:94: And the satraps and the commanders and the district governors and the king's officials gathered together and observed the men, that the fire had no power over their bodies, and the hair of their head was not singed, and their trousers were not altered, and there was no smell of fire on them.
verses.3:95: And Nebuchadnezzar answered and said, "Blessed be the God of Shadrach and Meshach and Abednego, who sent His angel and rescued His servants, because they trusted in Him; and they altered the king's word and handed over their bodies to fire, so that they might not serve nor worship any god except their God.
verses.3:96: And I issue the decree: 'Every people, tribe, language, if it speaks blasphemy against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, they will be for destruction and their houses for plunder, because there is no other god who will be able to deliver in this way.'"
verses.3:97: Then the king caused Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego to prosper in the province of Babylon, and deemed them worthy to lead all the Jews who were in his kingdom.
verses.4:4: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was prospering in my house and flourishing.
verses.4:5: I saw a dream, and it frightened me, and I was troubled on my bed, and the visions of my head greatly troubled me.
verses.4:10: On my bed I was watching, and look, a tree in the middle of the earth, and its height was great.
verses.4:11: The tree grew great and became strong, and its height reached to heaven, and its expanse to the end of all the earth.
verses.4:12: Its leaves were lovely, and its fruit was abundant, and food for all was in it; underneath it the wild beasts lodged, and in its branches the birds of the sky dwelt, and from it all flesh was fed.
verses.4:13: I was watching in a vision of the night on my bed, and look, a watcher and a holy one came down from heaven,
verses.4:14: and called out with strength, and thus he said, "Cut down the tree, and tear off its branches, and shake off its leaves, and scatter its fruit; let the beasts be dislodged from underneath it and the birds from its branches.
verses.4:15: Yet leave the stump of its roots in the earth, and in a band of iron and bronze, and in the green grass outside, and in the dew of heaven he will lie down, and his portion will be with the beasts in the grass of the earth.
verses.4:16: His heart will be altered away from humans, and a beast's heart will be given to him, and seven times will change over him.
verses.4:17: By the decree of a watcher is the word, and a saying of holy ones is the demand, so that the living may know that the Most High is Lord of the kingdom of humans, and to whomever He sees fit He will give it, and He will set up over it the most despised of humans."
verses.4:18: This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw; and you, Baltasar, tell the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to explain its interpretation to me; but you, Daniel, are able, because a holy spirit of God is in you.
verses.4:19: Then Daniel, whose name was Baltasar, was astounded for about one hour, and his thoughts greatly troubled him. And Baltasar answered and said, "Sir, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies.
verses.4:20: The tree that you saw, that grew great and was strong, whose height reached to heaven and its expanse to all the earth,
verses.4:21: and whose leaves were flourishing, and its fruit was abundant, and food for all was in it; underneath it the wild beasts dwelt, and in its branches the birds of the sky lodged;
verses.4:22: it is you, O king; for you have grown great and become strong, and your greatness has grown great and reached to heaven, and your dominion to the ends of the earth.
verses.4:23: And in that the king saw a watcher and a holy one coming down from heaven, and he said, 'Tear up the tree and destroy it, yet leave the stump of its roots in the earth, and in a band of iron and in bronze, and in the green grass outside, and in the dew of heaven he will pass the night, and with wild beasts his portion will be until seven times are altered over him';
verses.4:24: this is its interpretation, O king, and it is a decree of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king:
verses.4:25: and they will drive you away from humans, and your dwelling will be with wild beasts, and they will feed you grass like an ox, and from the dew of heaven you will pass the night, and seven times will change over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humans, and to whomever He sees fit He will give it.
verses.4:26: And in that they said, 'Leave the stump of the roots of the tree,' your kingdom will remain yours from the time you know the heavenly authority.
verses.4:27: Therefore, O king, let my counsel please you, and redeem your sins by acts of mercy, and your injustices by compassion for the poor; perhaps God will be patient toward your transgressions."
verses.4:28: All these things came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.4:29: After twelve months, while walking on the temple of his kingdom in Babylon,
verses.4:30: the king answered and said, "Is this not Babylon the great that I myself built for a royal house, by the might of my strength, for the honor of my glory?"
verses.4:31: While the word was still in the king's mouth, a voice came from heaven: "To you they speak, King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom has passed away from you,
verses.4:32: and they are driving you away from humans, and your dwelling will be with wild beasts, and they will feed you grass like an ox, and seven times will change over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humans, and to whomever He sees fit He will give it."
verses.4:33: In that very hour the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar, and he was driven away from humans, and he ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew long like lions' and his nails like birds'.
verses.4:34: And after the end of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and glorified Him who lives forever, because His authority is an everlasting authority and His kingdom is from generation to generation.
verses.4:36: At that very time my understanding returned to me, and I came into the honor of my kingdom; and my appearance returned to me, and my rulers and my nobles sought me out, and I was firmly established over my kingdom, and surpassing greatness was added to me.
verses.4:37: King Nebuchadnezzar to all the peoples, tribes, and languages who dwell in all the earth: May peace be multiplied to you. The signs and the wonders that the Most High God did with me, it has seemed good before me to declare to you. How great and mighty they are! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom; His authority is from generation to generation. Now therefore, I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, because all His works are true and His paths are justice, and all those who walk in pride He is able to humble.
verses.5:1: King Baltasar made a great feast for his thousand nobles, and before the thousand was the wine.
verses.5:2: And while drinking, Baltasar gave orders at the taste of his wine to bring the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar his father had brought out from the temple that was in Jerusalem, and let the king and his nobles and his concubines and his wives drink from them.
verses.5:3: And the gold and silver vessels were brought that he had brought out from the temple of God that was in Jerusalem, and the king and his nobles and his concubines and his wives drank from them;
verses.5:4: they drank wine, and praised the gods of gold and silver and bronze and iron and wood and stone.
verses.5:5: In that very hour fingers of a human hand came out and were writing opposite the lamp on the plaster of the wall and house of the king, and the king was watching the knuckles of the hand that was writing.
verses.5:6: Then the king's appearance was altered, and his thoughts greatly troubled him, and the joints of his waist were loosened, and his knees knocked together.
verses.5:7: And the king cried out with strength to bring in magicians, Chaldeans, diviners, and he said to the wise men of Babylon, "Whoever reads this writing and makes known its interpretation to me will be clothed in purple, and the gold collar will be on his neck, and he will rule as third in my kingdom."
verses.5:8: And all the king's wise men came in, and they were not able to read the writing nor to make known the interpretation to the king.
verses.5:9: And King Baltasar was troubled, and his appearance was altered within him, and his nobles were greatly troubled.
verses.5:10: And the queen entered the drinking hall and said, "O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts trouble you, and do not let your appearance be altered.
verses.5:11: There is a man in your kingdom in whom is a spirit of God, and in the days of your father watchfulness and understanding were found in him, and King Nebuchadnezzar your father appointed him chief of enchanters, magicians, Chaldeans, diviners,
verses.5:12: because an extraordinary spirit is in him, and wisdom and understanding—interpreting dreams and declaring hidden matters and loosening knots—Daniel, and the king gave him the name Baltasar; now therefore, let him be called, and he will declare its interpretation to you."
verses.5:13: Then Daniel was brought in before the king, and the king said to Daniel, "Are you Daniel, the one from the sons of the captivity of Judea, which the king my father brought?
verses.5:16: And I have heard about you, that you are able to interpret judgments; now therefore, if you are able to read the writing and make known its interpretation to me, you will be clothed in purple, and the gold collar will be on your neck, and you will rule as third in my kingdom."
verses.5:17: And Daniel said before the king, "Let your gifts be yours, and give the reward of your house to another; yet I will read the writing and make known its interpretation to you. And this is the writing that has been inscribed: 'Mane, Thekel, Phares.'
verses.5:23: And against the Lord God of heaven you exalted yourself, and you brought the vessels of His house before you, and you and your nobles and your concubines and your wives drank wine from them; and you praised the gods of gold and silver and bronze and iron and wood and stone, which do not see and which do not hear and do not know, but the God in whose hand is your breath and all your ways, Him you did not glorify.
verses.5:26: This is the interpretation of the word: 'Mane': God has measured your kingdom and brought it to an end;
verses.5:27: 'Thekel': it has been weighed on a balance and found lacking;
verses.5:28: 'Phares': your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and Persians."
verses.5:29: And Baltasar gave the command, and they clothed Daniel in purple, and they put the gold collar around his neck, and he proclaimed concerning him that he was third ruler in the kingdom.
verses.5:30: In that very night Baltasar the king of the Chaldeans was killed.
verses.6:1: And Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being sixty-two years old.
verses.6:2: And it was pleasing before Darius, and he appointed over the kingdom one hundred twenty satraps to be throughout all his kingdom,
verses.6:3: and over them three administrators, of whom Daniel was one, for the satraps to give account to them, so that the king would not be troubled.
verses.6:4: And Daniel was above them, because an extraordinary spirit was in him, and the king appointed him over his whole kingdom.
verses.6:5: And the administrators and the satraps were seeking to find a pretext against Daniel, and they found no pretext or offense or fault against him, because he was faithful.
verses.6:6: And the administrators said, "We will not find a pretext against Daniel except in the ordinances of his God."
verses.6:7: Then the administrators and the satraps presented themselves to the king and said to him, "King Darius, live forever!
verses.6:8: All the commanders and satraps, high officials and district governors over your kingdom have consulted together to establish a royal statute and to enforce an injunction, that whoever asks a petition from any god or man for thirty days except from you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.
verses.6:9: Now therefore, O king, establish the injunction and issue a written document, so that the decree of the Persians and Medes may not be altered."
verses.6:10: Then King Darius ordered the decree to be written.
verses.6:11: And Daniel, when he knew that the decree had been enacted, entered his house; and the windows were open for him in his upper chambers facing Jerusalem, and three times a day he was kneeling on his knees, and praying and giving thanks before his God, just as he had been doing previously.
verses.6:12: Then those men watched closely, and found Daniel petitioning and imploring his God.
verses.6:13: And they approached and said to the king, "O king, did you not ordain an injunction that every person who asks a petition from any god or man for thirty days except from you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions?" And the king said, "The word is true, and the decree of the Medes and Persians will not pass away."
verses.6:14: Then they answered and said before the king, "Daniel, from the sons of the captivity of Judea, has not submitted to your decree, and three times a day he asks his petitions from his God."
verses.6:15: Then the king, when he heard the matter, was deeply grieved over it, and strove concerning Daniel to rescue him.
verses.6:17: Then the king spoke, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions; and the king said to Daniel, "Your God, whom you serve continually, He Himself will rescue you."
verses.6:18: And they brought a stone and placed it over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his signet ring and with the signet ring of his nobles, so that nothing might be altered concerning Daniel.
verses.6:19: And the king went away to his house and lay down without supper, and they did not bring delicacies in to him, and sleep departed from him. And God shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not trouble Daniel.
verses.6:20: Then the king arose in the morning at daylight, and went in haste to the den of lions.
verses.6:21: And as he approached the den, he cried out with a loud voice, "Daniel, servant of the living God, was your God, whom you serve continually, able to rescue you from the mouth of the lions?"
verses.6:22: And Daniel said to the king, "Live forever, O king!
verses.6:23: My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not harm me, because before Him uprightness was found in me; and before you also, O king, I have committed no offense."
verses.6:24: Then the king was very glad over him, and ordered Daniel to be brought up out of the den. And Daniel was brought up out of the den, and no harm at all was found on him, because he trusted in his God.
verses.6:25: And the king spoke, and they brought the men who had accused Daniel, and they were thrown into the den of lions, they and their sons and their wives; and they had not reached the floor of the den before the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
verses.6:26: Then Darius the king wrote to all the peoples, tribes, languages dwelling in all the earth: "May peace be multiplied to you.
verses.6:27: From my presence this decree is issued, that in every dominion of my kingdom people are to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, for He is the living God and remains forever, and His kingdom will not be destroyed, and His sovereignty is to the end;
verses.6:28: He helps and delivers, and performs signs and wonders in heaven and on the earth, He who rescued Daniel from the hand of the lions."
verses.6:29: And Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
verses.7:1: In the third year of Belshazzar king of the Chaldeans, Daniel saw a dream and the visions of his head upon his bed, and he wrote down his dream.
verses.7:2: I, Daniel, was watching, and look, the four winds of heaven were striking against the great sea.
verses.7:3: And four great beasts were coming up out of the sea, differing from one another.
verses.7:4: The first was like a lioness, and it had wings like an eagle's; I was watching until its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the earth and stood on a man's feet, and a man's heart was given to it.
verses.7:5: And look, a second beast, resembling a bear, and it stood on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth; and thus they were saying to it, "Arise, eat much flesh."
verses.7:6: After this I was watching, and look, another beast like a leopard; and it had four wings of a bird above it, and the beast had four heads, and authority was given to it.
verses.7:7: After this I was watching, and look, a fourth beast, terrifying and dreadful and exceedingly strong, and its teeth were iron, eating and crushing, and it was trampling the remainder with its feet, and it was exceedingly different from all the beasts that were before it; and it had ten horns.
verses.7:8: I was considering its horns, and look, another small horn came up among them, and three of the horns before it were uprooted from its presence; and look, eyes like the eyes of a man were in this horn, and a mouth speaking great things.
verses.7:9: I was watching until thrones were placed, and the Ancient of Days was seated; His garment was white like snow, and the hair of His head like pure wool; His throne was a flame of fire, its wheels a blazing fire.
verses.7:10: A river of fire was flowing before Him; a thousand thousands were ministering to Him, and ten thousand myriads were standing before Him; a court sat, and books were opened.
verses.7:11: I was watching then because of the sound of the great words which that horn was speaking, until the beast was killed and perished, and its body was given to the burning of fire.
verses.7:12: And the dominion of the remaining beasts was removed, and a length of life was given to them for a time and a time.
verses.7:13: I was watching in a vision of the night, and look, with the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming, and reached the Ancient of Days, and was brought to Him.
verses.7:14: And to Him was given dominion and honor and kingdom, and all the peoples, tribes, and languages serve Him; His authority is an eternal authority that will not pass away, and His kingdom will not be destroyed.
verses.7:15: My spirit shuddered within my frame, I, Daniel, and the visions of my head were troubling me.
verses.7:16: And I approached one of those standing by, and was seeking the exact truth from him concerning all these things; and he told me the exact truth, and made known to me the interpretation of the words:
verses.7:17: "These four beasts are four kingdoms that will arise upon the earth, which will be taken away;
verses.7:18: and the holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever and ever."
verses.7:19: And I inquired closely concerning the fourth beast, because it was different from every beast, exceedingly terrifying, its teeth iron and its claws bronze, eating and crushing, and it was trampling the remainder with its feet;
verses.7:20: and concerning its ten horns that were on its head, and the other one that came up and shook off some of the first ones, which had the eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and its appearance was greater than the rest.
verses.7:21: I was watching, and that horn was making war with the holy ones, and prevailed against them,
verses.7:22: until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the holy ones of the Most High, and the time arrived and the holy ones took possession of the kingdom.
verses.7:23: And he said, "The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on the earth, which will surpass all the kingdoms, and will devour all the earth, and trample it down and cut it to pieces.
verses.7:24: And as for its ten horns, ten kings will arise; and after them one will arise who will surpass in evils all those before him, and he will humble three kings,
verses.7:25: and he will speak words against the Most High, and will wear out the holy ones of the Most High, and he will intend to alter times and law, and it will be given into his hand for a time and times and even half a time.
verses.7:26: And the court sat, and they will remove the dominion, to annihilate and to destroy it to the end,
verses.7:27: and the kingdom and the authority and the greatness of the kings under the whole heaven was given to the holy ones of the Most High; and His kingdom is an eternal kingdom, and all the dominions will serve and obey Him." Up to here is the end of the matter.
verses.7:28: As for me, Daniel, my thoughts were greatly troubling me, and my appearance was altered, and I kept the matter in my heart.
verses.8:1: In the third year of the reign of Belshazzar the king, a vision appeared to me—I, Daniel—after the one that appeared to me at the beginning.
verses.8:2: And I was in Susa the fortress, which is in the region of Elam, and I was by the Ubal.
verses.8:3: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, one ram standing before the Ubal, and it had high horns; and the one was higher than the other, and the high one was coming up last.
verses.8:4: I saw the ram butting toward the sea and north and south; and none of the beasts will stand before it, and there was no one rescuing from its hand, and it did according to its will and became great.
verses.8:5: And I was considering, and look, a male goat was coming from the west over the face of all the earth, and it was not touching the earth; and the male goat had a horn between its eyes.
verses.8:6: And it came up to the ram that had the horns, which I had seen standing before the Ubal, and it ran toward it in the rush of its strength.
verses.8:7: And I saw it reaching up to the ram, and it became enraged against it; and it struck the ram and shattered both of its horns, and the ram had no strength to stand before it; and it threw it to the earth and trampled it, and there was no one rescuing the ram from its hand.
verses.8:8: And the male goat became exceedingly great; and when it had grown strong, its great horn was shattered, and four horns came up underneath it toward the four winds of heaven.
verses.8:9: And out of one of them came forth one strong horn, and it became extraordinarily great toward the south and toward the host;
verses.8:10: it became great, up to the host of heaven; and some of the host of heaven and some of the stars fell to the earth, and they trampled them,
verses.8:11: and until the chief commander delivers the captivity, and because of him sacrifice was dashed down, and it prospered for him; and the sanctuary will be made desolate.
verses.8:12: And sin was given over the sacrifice, and righteousness was thrown to the ground; and it acted and prospered.
verses.8:13: And I heard a holy one speaking; and one holy one said to Phelmuni who was speaking, "How long will the vision stand—the sacrifice that was taken away and the sin of desolation that was given—and the sanctuary and the host be trampled?"
verses.8:14: And he said to him, "Until evening and morning, two thousand three hundred days; and the sanctuary will be cleansed."
verses.8:15: And it happened, when I, Daniel, saw the vision, that I was seeking understanding; and look, there stood before me one like the appearance of a man.
verses.8:16: And I heard a man's voice in the midst of the Ubal, and he called out and said, "Gabriel, make that one understand the vision."
verses.8:17: And he came and stood next to where I stood; and when he came, I was terrified, and I fell on my face; and he said to me, "Son of man, for the vision is still for the end of time."
verses.8:18: And while he was speaking with me, I fell on my face to the earth, and he touched me and set me on my feet,
verses.8:19: and he said, "Look, I am making known to you the things that will be at the end of the wrath; for the vision is still for the end of time.
verses.8:20: The ram that you saw, the one having the horns, is the king of the Persians and Medes.
verses.8:21: And the male goat is the king of the Greeks; and the great horn that was between its eyes, he is the first king.
verses.8:22: And as for the one that was shattered, where four horns stood underneath, four kings from his nation will arise, and not in their strength.
verses.8:23: And at the end of their kingdom, when their sins are filled up, a king will arise, shameless in face and understanding riddles.
verses.8:24: And his strength will be mighty, and he will destroy astonishingly, and he will succeed and act, and he will destroy strong ones and a holy people.
verses.8:25: And the yoke of his collar will succeed; deceit is in his hand, and in his heart he will make himself great, and by deceit he will destroy many, and he will stand over the destruction of many, and like eggs he will shatter by hand.
verses.8:26: And the vision of the evening and of the morning that was spoken of is true; and you, seal up the vision, for it is for many days."
verses.8:27: And I, Daniel, slept and was sick; and I got up and was doing the king's work, and I was astonished at the vision, and there was no one who understood.
verses.9:1: In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, who became king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
verses.9:2: I, Daniel, understood in the books the number of the years, concerning which the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet for the completion of the desolation of Jerusalem, seventy years.
verses.9:3: And I set my face toward the Lord God to seek prayer and supplications in fastings and sackcloth.
verses.9:4: And I prayed to the Lord my God and made confession and said, "Lord God, the great and wondrous One, who keeps Your covenant and mercy for those who love You and for those who keep Your commandments,
verses.9:5: we have sinned, we have committed iniquity, we have acted lawlessly, and we have rebelled and turned aside from Your commandments and from Your judgments;
verses.9:6: and we have not listened to Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings and our rulers and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.
verses.9:7: To You, Lord, belongs righteousness, and to us belongs shame of face, as on this day, to the man of Judah and to those dwelling in Jerusalem and to all Israel, those who are near and those who are far off in every land where You scattered them, because of their treachery with which they acted treacherously.
verses.9:8: In You, Lord, is our righteousness, and to us belongs shame of face, and to our kings and to our rulers and to our fathers, who have sinned against You.
verses.9:9: To the Lord our God belong compassions and pardons, because we have rebelled,
verses.9:10: and we have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God to walk in His laws, which He placed before our face by the hands of His servants the prophets.
verses.9:11: And all Israel have transgressed Your law and turned aside so as not to hear Your voice; and the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses, the servant of God, came upon us, because we sinned against Him.
verses.9:12: And He established His words which He spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, to bring upon us great evils, such as have not happened under all heaven like what happened in Jerusalem.
verses.9:13: Just as it is written in the law of Moses, all these evils came upon us; yet we did not entreat the face of the Lord our God to turn back from our iniquities and to understand in all Your truth.
verses.9:14: And the Lord kept watch and brought them upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in all His work that He has done, and we have not listened to His voice.
verses.9:15: And now, Lord our God, who brought Your people out from the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made for Yourself a name as on this day, we have sinned, we have acted lawlessly.
verses.9:16: Lord, in all Your mercy, please let Your anger and Your wrath turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; because we have sinned, and in our iniquities and those of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people have become a reproach among all those around us.
verses.9:17: And now listen, Lord our God, to the prayer of Your servant and to his supplications, and make Your face shine upon Your desolate sanctuary for Your own sake, Lord.
verses.9:18: Incline, my God, Your ear and hear; open Your eyes and see our ruin and that of Your city upon which Your name has been called; for not upon our righteous deeds do we cast our compassion before You, but upon Your many compassions, Lord.
verses.9:19: Listen, Lord! Pardon, Lord! Pay attention, Lord! Do not delay for Your own sake, my God, because Your name has been called upon Your city and upon Your people."
verses.9:20: Now while I was still speaking and praying, and confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel, and casting my mercy before the Lord my God concerning the holy mountain,
verses.9:21: even while I was still speaking in prayer, look, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, was flying, and he touched me about the hour of the evening sacrifice.
verses.9:22: And he gave me understanding, and spoke with me and said, "Daniel, now I have come out to instruct you in understanding.
verses.9:23: At the beginning of your supplication a word went out, and I have come to tell you, because you are a man greatly desired; so consider the message and understand the vision.
verses.9:24: Seventy weeks have been determined upon your people and upon the holy city, for sin to be ended, and to seal up sins and to blot out the iniquities, and to make atonement for iniquity, and to bring in eternal righteousness, and to seal up vision and prophet, and to anoint a holy of holies.
verses.9:25: And you will know and understand: from the going out of a word to answer and to build Jerusalem until an anointed one, a ruler, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks; and it will return and be built, plaza and wall, and the times will be emptied out.
verses.9:26: And after the sixty-two weeks, anointing will be utterly destroyed, and there is no judgment in it; and he will destroy the city and the sanctuary with the ruler who is coming; they will be cut off in a flood, and until the end of a determined war, there will be ruins by decree.
verses.9:27: And one week will confirm a covenant for many; and in the half of the week My sacrifice and drink offering will be taken away, and upon the temple will be an abomination of desolations, and until the end of time, an end will be given upon the desolation."
verses.10:1: In the third year of Cyrus king of the Persians, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the word is true, and great power and understanding were given to him in the vision.
verses.10:2: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three weeks of days.
verses.10:3: I did not eat desirable bread, and meat and wine did not enter into my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with ointment, until the completion of three weeks of days.
verses.10:4: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was beside the great river, that is, Tigris Hiddekel.
verses.10:5: And I lifted up my eyes and looked, and look, one man clothed in baddin, and his waist was girded with gold of Uphaz,
verses.10:6: and his body was like tharsis, and his face was like the appearance of lightning, and his eyes were like torches of fire, and his arms and legs were like the appearance of gleaming bronze, and the sound of his words was like the sound of a multitude.
verses.10:7: And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision, and the men who were with me did not see the vision; yet a great terror fell upon them, and they fled in fear.
verses.10:8: And I alone was left, and I saw this great vision, and no strength was left in me, and my glory was turned into ruin, and I retained no strength.
verses.10:9: And I heard the sound of his words, and when I heard him, I was stunned, with my face to the ground.
verses.10:10: And look, a hand was touching me, and it raised me onto my knees.
verses.10:11: And he said to me, "Daniel, man of delight, understand the words that I am speaking to you, and stand in your place, for now I have been sent to you." And when he spoke this word to me, I stood up trembling.
verses.10:12: And he said to me, "Do not fear, Daniel; for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to afflict yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come because of your words.
verses.10:13: And the prince of the kingdom of the Persians stood against me for twenty-one days; and look, Michael, one of the princes, came to help me, and I left him there with the prince of the kingdom of the Persians.
verses.10:14: And I have come to give you understanding of what will happen to your people in the last days, for the vision is yet for days."
verses.10:15: And when he spoke with me according to these words, I set my face upon the ground.
verses.10:16: And look, one like the likeness of a son of man touched my lips; and I opened my mouth and spoke, and I said to the one standing before me, "My lord, in your vision my inward parts turned within me, and I had no strength.
verses.10:17: And how will your servant, my lord, be able to speak with this lord of mine? And as for me, from now on no strength will stand in me, and no breath was left in me."
verses.10:18: And one like the appearance of a man touched me again, and strengthened me,
verses.10:19: and said to me, "Do not fear, man of delight; peace to you; be courageous and be strong." And when he spoke with me, I grew strong, and I said, "Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me."
verses.10:20: And he said, "Do you know why I have come to you? And now I will return to fight against the prince of the Persians; and I was going in, and the prince of the Greeks was coming.
verses.10:21: Yet I will declare to you what is inscribed in the writing of truth, and there is not one holding fast with me concerning these things except Michael your prince."
verses.11:1: "And I, in the first year of Cyrus, stood for might and strength.
verses.11:2: And now I will declare the truth to you: look, three more kings will arise in Persia, and the fourth will become rich with great wealth beyond all; and after he has gained mastery of his wealth, he will rise up against all the kingdoms of the Greeks.
verses.11:3: And a mighty king will arise, and he will rule over a great dominion, and he will act according to his will.
verses.11:4: And as soon as he stands, his kingdom will be shattered and divided toward the four winds of heaven, and not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion that he ruled; for his kingdom will be plucked up, and for others besides these.
verses.11:5: And the king of the south will grow strong; and one of their princes will grow strong over them and will rule a great dominion.
verses.11:6: And after his years they will join together, and the daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make a treaty with him; and she will not retain strength of arm, and his seed will not stand, and she will be handed over, and those who bring her, and the young woman, and the one who strengthens her in those times.
verses.11:7: And one from the blossom of her root, of his position, will stand, and he will come to the army, and he will enter into the strongholds of the king of the north, and he will act against them and prevail.
verses.11:8: And indeed their gods with their cast images, every desirable vessel of theirs, of silver and gold, he will carry with captivity into Egypt; and he will stand above the king of the north.
verses.11:9: And he will come into the kingdom of the king of the south, and he will return into his own land.
verses.11:10: And his sons will gather a multitude among many, and he will indeed come and overflow, and he will pass through and settle down and engage in conflict as far as his strength.
verses.11:11: And the king of the south will be enraged, and he will go out and fight against the king of the north, and he will raise up a great multitude, and a multitude will be handed over into his hand;
verses.11:12: and he will take the multitude, and his heart will be lifted up, and he will cast down tens of thousands, yet he will not prevail.
verses.11:13: And the king of the north will return and bring a great multitude beyond the former, and at the end of the times of years he will come with supplies, with a great army and with many possessions.
verses.11:14: And in those times many will rise up against the king of the south, and the sons of the remnant of your people will lift themselves up to establish a vision, and they will grow weak.
verses.11:15: And the king of the north will enter, and he will pour out a siege mound and capture fortified cities; and the arms of the king of the south will stand, and his chosen ones also will rise up, and there will be no strength to stand.
verses.11:16: And the one who comes against him will do according to his will, and there is no one standing before him; and he will stand in the land of Sabeir, and it will be accomplished in his hand.
verses.11:17: And he will set his face to enter with the strength of all his kingdom, and he will make all things straight with him; and he will give him a daughter of women to ruin her, yet she will not remain, and she will not be for him.
verses.11:18: And he will turn his face to the islands and capture many, and he will put an end to the princes of their reproach; yet his reproach will return to him.
verses.11:19: And he will turn his face toward the strength of his own land, and he will grow weak and fall, and he will not be found.
verses.11:20: And there will arise from his root a plant of the kingdom in his position, causing to pass over, exacting the glory of the kingdom; and in those days he will be shattered, yet not in faces, nor in battle.
verses.11:21: One will stand in his position; he was despised, and they did not bestow the glory of the kingdom on him; yet he will come in prosperity, and he will gain control of the kingdom through slippery schemes.
verses.11:22: And the arms of the one who floods will be flooded away from before him and will be shattered, along with a leader of a covenant.
verses.11:23: And from the alliances with him he will practice deceit, and he will go up and overpower them with a small nation.
verses.11:24: And in prosperity and in rich regions he will come, and he will do what his fathers and the fathers of his fathers did not do; plunder and spoil and possessions he will scatter among them, and against Egypt he will devise plans, even until a time.
verses.11:25: And his strength and his heart will be stirred up against the king of the south with a great army, and the king of the south will join battle with a great and exceedingly strong army; and they will not stand, because they will devise plans against him.
verses.11:26: And they will eat his provisions and shatter him, and he will flood armies, and many wounded will fall.
verses.11:27: And as for both kings, their hearts are set on evil, and at one table they will speak lies, but it will not succeed; for the end is yet for a time.
verses.11:28: And he will return to his own land with many possessions, and his heart will be against the holy covenant; and he will act, and he will return to his own land.
verses.11:29: At the appointed time he will return and come into the south, and it will not be like the first and the last.
verses.11:30: And the Kittim who go out will come against him, and he will be humbled; and he will return and become enraged against the holy covenant, and he will act and return, and he will pay attention to those who forsake the holy covenant.
verses.11:31: And seeds from him will rise up, and they will profane the sanctuary of power, and remove the continual offering, and set up an abomination made desolate.
verses.11:32: And those who act lawlessly against the covenant will lead on with slippery schemes; and a people knowing its God will prevail and act,
verses.11:33: and those of the people who have understanding will understand in many things, yet they will grow weak by sword and by flame, and by captivity and by plundering for days.
verses.11:34: And when they grow weak, they will be helped with a little help, and many will join themselves to them with slippery schemes.
verses.11:35: And some of those who have understanding will grow weak, in order to refine them and to choose and to be revealed until a time's end; for it is yet for a time.
verses.11:36: And he will do according to his will; and the king will exalt himself and magnify himself above every god, and he will speak arrogant things, and he will succeed until the wrath is completed; for it comes to completion.
verses.11:37: And to any god of his fathers he will pay no attention, nor to the desire of women, nor to any god will he pay attention; for he will magnify himself above all.
verses.11:38: And the god Maozein in his place he will glorify, and a god whom his fathers did not know he will glorify with gold and silver and precious stone and with desirable things.
verses.11:39: And he will deal with the strongholds of the refuges with a foreign god, and he will multiply glory, and he will subject many to them, and he will divide land for gifts.
verses.11:40: And at the end of a time he will lock horns with the king of the south, and the king of the north will be gathered against him with chariots and horsemen and with many ships; and they will enter into the land, and he will shatter and pass through.
verses.11:41: And he will enter into the land of Sabaein, and many will grow weak; yet these will be rescued out of his hand: Edom and Moab and the chief of the sons of Ammon.
verses.11:42: And he will stretch out his hand against the land, and the land of Egypt will not be for deliverance.
verses.11:43: And he will rule over the hidden treasures of gold and silver, and over all the desirable things of Egypt and of the Libyans and of the Ethiopians, in their strongholds.
verses.11:44: And reports and urgencies will trouble him from the east and from the north, and he will come with great fury to destroy many.
verses.11:45: And he will pitch his tent Ephadano between the seas, at the holy mountain of Sabaein; and he will come to his portion, and there is no one who delivers him."
verses.12:1: And at that time Michael, the great prince, the one who stands over the sons of your people, will arise; and there will be a time of affliction, affliction such as has not occurred since a nation has existed on the earth until that time. At that time your people will be saved, everyone who is written in the book.
verses.12:2: And many of those sleeping in the dust of the earth will be awakened, these to eternal life, and those to reproach and to eternal shame.
verses.12:3: And those who understand will shine like the brilliance of the expanse, and some from among the many righteous, like the stars forever and beyond.
verses.12:4: And you, Daniel, close up the rest and seal the book until the time of the end, until many are taught and knowledge is multiplied.
verses.12:5: And I, Daniel, saw, and look, two others were standing, one on this side of the bank of the river and one on that side of the bank of the river.
verses.12:6: And he said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the water of the river, "How long until the end of the wonders that you have spoken?"
verses.12:7: And I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the water of the river, and he raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven, and he swore by the One who lives forever, "For a time of times and half a time; when scattering is completed, they will know all these things."
verses.12:8: And I heard and did not understand, and I said, "Lord, what is the final outcome of these things?"
verses.12:9: And he said, "Come, Daniel, for the words are closed up and sealed until the end of the time,
verses.12:10: until many are chosen and made white and refined, and lawless ones act lawlessly; and lawless ones will not understand, and the discerning will understand.
verses.12:11: And from the time of the removal of the continual offering, an abomination of desolation will be given, one thousand two hundred ninety days.
verses.12:12: Blessed is the one who endures and arrives at one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
verses.12:13: And you, come and rest; for there are still days until the fulfillment of the end, and you will arise to your allotted share at the end of days."

notes.1:2: The Greek uses the genitive "of the house of his god" (οἴκου τοῦ θεοῦ αὐτοῦ) without a preposition after "the land of Shinar," linking the temple with the land rather than marking a second destination as in the Hebrew MT ("to the house of his god").
notes.1:3: Preserves trailing comma continuing into v. 4.
notes.1:5: Here and in verses 8, 13, and 15, the Greek consistently reads "the king's table" (τράπεζα) where the Hebrew MT has "the king's choice food" (pat-bag); verses 13 and 15 literally read "eat the king's table."
notes.1:11: The Greek treats the Hebrew title hammelsar ("the steward" or "the overseer") as the personal name "Amelsad" (Ἀμελσάδ; spelled Ἁμελσάδ in v. 16).
notes.1:12: The Greek renders the Hebrew term for vegetable or pulse fare literally as "seeds" (σπερμάτων; also σπέρματα in v. 16), denoting plant foods grown from seed.
notes.2:1: The Saints Greek text of Daniel is the Theodotion version. ἐξέστη ("was beside itself, distraught") is rendered "distraught" here and in 2:3. The Greek spells the king's name Ναβουχοδονοσόρ; the standard English Nebuchadnezzar is used.
notes.2:4: Συριστί is literally "in Syrian," the usual Greek term for Aramaic. It is rendered "in Aramaic" so the meaning is clear. In the Hebrew Bible the text itself switches to Aramaic at this point.
notes.2:5: Ὁ λόγος ἀπ᾽ ἐμοῦ ἀπέστη ("the word has departed from me") is kept literal. It may mean that the king has forgotten the dream or that his decree is final.
notes.2:10: The Greek uses the historical present (λέγουσιν, "they say"). It is rendered with the English past for smooth narrative, here and in 2:27.
notes.2:14: ἀρχιμάγειρος means literally "chief cook" (or chief butcher), a court title that came to mean the captain of the royal guard. The literal title is kept.
notes.2:20: ἀπὸ τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἕως τοῦ αἰῶνος, "from the age and until the age," is rendered "from age to age."
notes.2:26: The Greek spells the name Βαλτασάρ (Baltasar). The standard English form Belteshazzar, Daniel's Babylonian name, is used.
notes.2:27: γαζαρηνῶν ("Gazarenes") transliterates the Aramaic word for "diviners" or "determiners of fate." It is rendered by its meaning.
notes.2:37: Verses 37–38 form one sentence in the Greek, with no main verb for "You, King, king of kings"; the structure is kept.
notes.2:44: ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ uses a masculine pronoun, which cannot refer to the feminine βασιλεία, so it is taken as "His (God's) kingdom." λικμάω means "winnow, scatter like chaff."
notes.2:46: μαννά here is the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew/Aramaic word for a grain offering (minchah), not the wilderness manna. It is rendered "an offering." σπεῖσαι is "to pour out (as a libation)."
notes.3:1: The Greek text opens with the date "In the eighteenth year" (absent in the Aramaic text) and reads the place name "Deira" (corresponding to Aramaic "Dura").
notes.3:15: Greek "symphonia" (a musical instrument, probably a bagpipe or ensemble) appears in the Greek text here, whereas it is omitted in the parallel lists of vv. 5, 7, and 10.
notes.3:17: The Greek reads "For there is a God, whom we serve, able to rescue us" (or "For God, whom we serve, is able"), without the conditional clause and possessive "our" found in the Aramaic text.
notes.3:24: Verses 24–47 (continuing further in the chapter) form part of the Greek-only addition containing the Prayer of Azariah and the expanded narrative of the furnace.
notes.3:40: The clause "and carry through completely after You" (Greek: kai ektelesai opisthen sou) is grammatically difficult and likely expresses wholehearted persistence in following God.
notes.3:61: The Greek reads singular "all the host" (Greek: pasa he dynamis) without "of the Lord," followed by plural imperatives in the second half of the verse.
notes.3:72: In this Greek versification (with vv. 67–70 omitted from the numbering), v. 72 combines three refrains ("light and darkness," "cold and heat," and "frost and snow").
notes.3:92: The Greek begins Nebuchadnezzar's statement directly without an introductory "he answered and said," and reads "like a son of God" (Greek: hyio theou, singular without the article).
notes.3:97: The closing clause ("and deemed them worthy to lead all the Jews who were in his kingdom") is a Greek-only expansion absent from the Aramaic text.
notes.4:13: Greek εἲρ (eir) is an untranslated transliteration of Aramaic 'ir ("watcher," an angelic being); in 4:17 the form lacks a plural ending (cf. MT plural "watchers").
notes.4:18: Greek uses Baltasar (transliterating Aramaic Belteshazzar) for Daniel's Babylonian name, identical to the king's name in chapter 5, and reads singular "a holy spirit of God" (cf. MT "spirit of the holy gods").
notes.4:27: Greek reads "perhaps God will be patient toward your transgressions," differing from the Aramaic MT ("perhaps there will be a lengthening of your prosperity").
notes.4:29: Greek ναῷ ("temple") translates Aramaic hekela', which can mean either "temple" or "palace."
notes.4:33: Greek reads "like lions'" (leonton) where the Aramaic MT has "like eagles'." Also note that 4:37 concludes the chapter with Nebuchadnezzar's greeting and doxology (paralleling MT 4:1-3), while MT 4:6-9 and 4:35 are absent in this Greek text.
notes.5:1: Greek uses Baltasar for King Belshazzar (the same spelling as Daniel's Babylonian name in 4:18-19 and 5:12) and concludes the verse with the verbless clause "before the thousand was the wine."
notes.5:7: Greek γαζαρηνούς (gazarenoi, also in 5:11) transliterates Aramaic gazerin ("diviners" or "astrologers").
notes.5:11: Greek γρηγόρησις ("watchfulness" or "alertness") reflects a reading related to wakefulness where the Aramaic MT has "illumination/insight."
notes.5:17: Greek reads three inscribed words ("Mane, Thekel, Phares") rather than the Aramaic MT's four ("Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin"); verses 5:14-15, 5:18-22, and 5:24-25 of the MT are absent from this Greek text.
notes.5:27: Greek ὑστεροῦσα is feminine singular ("it [your kingdom] ... found lacking"), whereas the Aramaic MT addresses the king directly in the second person ("you have been weighed ... and found deficient").
notes.6:4: Unlike the Aramaic tradition ("planned to appoint"), the Greek text uses the indicative κατέστησεν ("appointed"), stating that the king actually appointed Daniel over his whole kingdom.
notes.6:15: The Greek text moves directly from the king's distress and effort to rescue Daniel in 6:15 to his command in 6:17, omitting the phrase "until sunset" and verse 16 (the conspirators' second appeal in the Aramaic tradition).
notes.6:19: The final sentence ("And God shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not trouble Daniel") stands in the Greek text here but is absent from the Aramaic tradition.
notes.6:21: The Greek reads "from the mouth of the lions" (ἐκ στόματος τῶν λεόντων), whereas the Aramaic has simply "from the lions."
notes.7:1: The Greek text dates this vision to the "third" year of Belshazzar "king of the Chaldeans," whereas the Aramaic tradition reads the "first" year of Belshazzar "king of Babylon" and includes "the sum of the matters" before he wrote the dream.
notes.7:17: The Greek identifies the four beasts as "four kingdoms" (rather than "four kings" as in the Aramaic) and includes the closing clause "which will be taken away" (αἳ ἀρθήσονται).
notes.7:20: Unlike the Aramaic ("before which three fell"), the Greek omits the number "three" and uses the active participle ἐκτινάξαντος ("shook off") with the partitive genitive τῶν πρώτων ("some of the first ones").
notes.7:24: Where the Aramaic reads "he will be different from the former ones," the Greek text has ὃς ὑπεροίσει κακοῖς πάντας τοὺς ἔμπροσθεν ("who will surpass in evils all those before him").
notes.7:27: The Greek reads "of the kings" (τῶν βασιλέων) rather than "of the kingdoms," and the angel's speech ends before the closing editorial sentence ("Up to here is the end of the matter"), which stands at the beginning of verse 28 in the Aramaic tradition.
notes.8:2: The Greek reads "the Ubal" (τοῦ Οὐβάλ), treating the Hebrew common noun ubal ("canal/stream") as a proper name corresponding to "the Ulai" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, and omits the Hebrew clause "and I saw in the vision."
notes.8:9: The Greek reads "one strong horn" (ἰσχυρόν) rather than "one little horn" as in Hebrew, and reads "toward the south and toward the host" (τὴν δύναμιν) without Hebrew's "toward the east" and "beautiful land."
notes.8:11: The Greek differs notably from the Hebrew here, reading "until the chief commander delivers the captivity" (vs. Hebrew "even up to the prince of the host it magnified itself") and "because of him sacrifice was dashed down (ἐράχθη), and it prospered for him."
notes.8:13: "Phelmuni" (φελμουνεί) is a Greek transliteration of Hebrew palmoni ("a certain one"), retained as a name or title for the speaking angelic figure; the Greek also reads "sin of desolation that was given" and omits "regular/daily" before "sacrifice."
notes.8:25: The Greek reads "the yoke of his collar" (vs. Hebrew "his cunning"), "over the destruction of many" (vs. Hebrew "against the Prince of princes"), and "like eggs he will shatter by hand" (vs. Hebrew "without hand he will be broken").
notes.9:8: The Greek preserves an opening confession ("In You, Lord, is our righteousness") that is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.9:24: The Greek contains seven infinitive purpose clauses (adding "and to blot out the iniquities") rather than six as in Hebrew, and reads singular "prophet" (προφήτην) rather than "prophecy."
notes.9:25: Notable Greek readings here include "to answer" (τοῦ ἀποκριθῆναι, vs. Hebrew "to restore"), "an anointed one, a ruler" (χριστοῦ ἡγουμένου), and "the times will be emptied out" (ἐκκενωθήσονται οἱ καιροί, vs. Hebrew "in troubled times").
notes.9:26: The Greek reads neuter "anointing" (χρίσμα, corresponding to Hebrew "anointed one"), "there is no judgment in it" (vs. Hebrew "and have nothing"), "with (σύν) the ruler who is coming" (reading Hebrew as "with" rather than "people of"), and "ruins by decree" (τάξει ἀφανισμοί).
notes.9:27: In Greek, "one week" (ἑβδομὰς μία) stands in the nominative as the grammatical subject of "will confirm" (or as an adverbial time phrase), "My sacrifice" includes the first-person pronoun μου ("My"), and "upon the temple" (ἐπὶ τὸ ἱερόν) corresponds to Hebrew "upon the wing of abominations."
notes.10:1: Greek reads Baltasar (the Septuagint/Theodotion form used for both Belteshazzar and Belshazzar), and renders "great power and understanding were given to him" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a great conflict."
notes.10:4: Greek uniquely combines both river names, Tigris and Hiddekel (Eddekel), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text mentions only Hiddekel.
notes.10:5: "baddin" is an untranslated Greek transliteration of Hebrew baddim, meaning linen garments.
notes.10:6: "tharsis" is an untranslated Greek transliteration of Hebrew tarshish, referring to a golden gemstone such as chrysolite or beryl.
notes.10:13: Greek has active "I left him [Michael] there with the prince of the kingdom of the Persians" and omits "chief" before "princes" (contrasting with MT "I was left there beside the kings of Persia"); similarly in v. 20, Greek reads "I was going in" rather than "going out."
notes.11:1: Greek names Cyrus here, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Darius the Mede.
notes.11:15: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("will not stand"), Greek has no negative particle before "will stand" (v. 15); in v. 16, Greek turns "the glorious land" into a place name, Sabeir (spelled Sabaein in vv. 41, 45).
notes.11:20: Greek adds "a plant of the kingdom," translates the sending of an exactor with the participles "causing to pass over, exacting," and renders Hebrew appayim ("anger/faces") literally as "in faces."
notes.11:31: Greek reads "seeds" (from Hebrew zera'im rather than MT zero'im, "arms/forces") and uses a passive participle ("made desolate") for the abomination; in v. 30, Greek reads "the Kittim who go out" where MT has "ships of Kittim."
notes.11:38: Greek leaves Maozein (Heb. ma'uzzim, "fortresses") untranslated as the name of a god; similarly in v. 45, Ephadano (Heb. appadno, "his palatial tents") is treated as a place name, and "his portion" (Greek merous) stands where MT reads "his end."
notes.12:3: The Greek literally reads "from among the many righteous" (apo ton dikaion ton pollon) rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "those who lead the many to righteousness," and renders the closing phrase as "forever and beyond" (eis tous aionas kai eti).
notes.12:4: The Greek text reads tous loipous ("the rest," a notable variant for tous logous, "the words"; cf. v. 9) and has "until many are taught" (didachthosin polloi) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "many will run to and fro."
notes.12:7: Greek literally reads "for a time of times" (kairon kairon, genitive plural) and omits the Hebrew phrase "the power of the holy people" after "scattering" (diaskorpismon). It also reads "they will know all these things" (gnosontai) where the Masoretic Text has "all these things will be finished," while "water" (vv. 6-7) is singular and "linen" translates the Hebrew loanword ta baddein.
notes.12:10: This Greek text leaves v. 9 open without final punctuation so that "until" (heos) in v. 9 governs the aorist subjunctives in v. 10; eklegosin literally means "be chosen" rather than "be purified."
notes.12:13: The clause "for there are still days until the fulfillment of the end" is present in the Greek text though absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, and deuro (also in v. 9) literally means "come."
